title: Graphs and Transformations
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Graphs and Transformations Worksheets
standard_text: Understand the effect of simple transformations on the graph of y = f(x), including sketching associated graphs: y = af(x), y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = f(ax).
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on graphs and transformations: translations, stretches and reflections of y = f(x) and transforming points. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: f(x + a): left a. f(x) + a: up a.
key_sub: af(x) stretches vertically; f(ax) stretches horizontally by 1/a.
body_html:
How it works

y = f(x) + a moves the graph up a; y = f(x + a) moves it left a. y = af(x) is a vertical stretch, scale factor a; y = f(ax) is a horizontal stretch, scale factor 1/a. −f(x) reflects in the x-axis, f(−x) in the y-axis.

Example

(2, 5) on y = f(x). Image on y = f(x − 3) + 1?

Right 3, up 1

Answer: (5, 6)

Example

(4, 3) on y = f(x). Image on y = f(2x)?

Halve the x-coordinate

Answer: (2, 3)

Common mistakes

  • Moving right for f(x + a).
  • Using scale factor a (not 1/a) for f(ax).
  • Mixing up the two reflections.

faq.q: What does y = f(x + a) do?
faq.a: It translates the graph by a units to the left (the vector (−a, 0)).
It is a horizontal stretch with scale factor 1/a, so x-coordinates are divided by a.
